name: Akumal
line: Turtle bay, cenotes and reef

key_facts: Akumal means 'place of the turtles' in Maya; the bay's seagrass beds feed wild green sea turtles.
A certified guide and life jacket are mandatory to enter the turtle-snorkel area.
No touching turtles (federal offense); keep 3 m distance, 2 min per turtle, biodegradable sunscreen or rashguard only.
Turtle sightings permitted 8am-5pm; sessions cap at ~55 minutes; no fins, no diving on the circuit.
Cenote and reef diving are easily reached, making Akumal a serene dive base.

safety.hospital: Nearest trauma: Hospiten Riviera Maya, Playa del Carmen (+52 984 159 2200), ~25 min north; local clinics stabilize/transfer; major trauma to Cancún
safety.yellow_fever: none required

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Akumal?
faq.a: Sargassum, water, mosquitoes and hurricanes — not violent crime. 2026 is tracking a record sargassum year, with Akumal affected Apr–Aug (Jun–Jul peak) because the bay is seagrass habitat and naturally weedy by design; drink bottled/purified water only, use repellent for dengue (peak May–November, no malaria), and note hurricane season runs June–November.

faq.q: Can you swim with wild sea turtles in Akumal, and when's best?
faq.a: Yes — it is the whole reason to come, and green turtles graze the bay's seagrass year-round. Go at 8am opening for the calmest water and fewest boats; snorkeling is permitted only 8am–5pm in sessions capped at ~55 minutes, always with a certified guide over the seagrass beds.

faq.q: Can I dive cenotes and reef from Akumal?
faq.a: Yes — Akumal makes a serene dive base for both. Guided cenote cavern dives sit just inland (Cenote Azul corridor) and shallow reef dives are close to shore; cavern diving requires a certified cave/cavern guide and stays in the daylight zone. Observe no-fly of 18h single / 24h repetitive; the nearest chamber is ~25 min north in Playa del Carmen.

faq.q: Is Akumal good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, if you want quiet and private over resort buzz. Akumal is villa-driven — beachfront villas with private pools and chef service, plus the wider luxury tier at ~US$400–600+/night in March — and it is calmer and more purposeful than Playa or Tulum. For branded ultra, Rosewood/Banyan Tree at Mayakoba sit ~35–40 min north with an easy turtle-morning day trip.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Akumal, and when is it cheapest?
faq.a: Nov–March is the best weather window; the cheapest is the green season, June–mid-October. Peak Dec–Apr brings the best conditions and highest rates; May–June and November shoulders run ~30–40% off with thinner crowds; the green season is hot, rainy and cheapest but carries hurricane exposure (Jun–Nov).

faq.q: Can I visit Maya ruins from Akumal?
faq.a: Yes — Akumal pairs a turtle morning with cliff-top Maya ruins in a single day. Tulum's ruins are a short drive south and Cobá is inland; a common loop is ruins at 8–10am then the turtle bay after, bookable as a guided combo excursion.

faq.q: What is the best diving and snorkeling on Ambergris Caye?
faq.a: Start at Hol Chan Marine Reserve and Shark Ray Alley. The signature ~30-ft channel dive delivers moray, turtles and 160+ fish species, while Shark Ray Alley — added as Zone D in 1999 — puts you in shallow water with docile 4–6 ft nurse sharks and southern stingrays. Both are guided, beginner-friendly profiles because they are shallow and protected.

faq.q: Do you need a car on Ambergris Caye?
faq.a: No — the island runs on golf carts, not cars, and beachfront San Pedro properties sit a 10-minute walk from the airstrip and steps from the water-taxi dock. English is the official language (Belize is the only English-official nation in Central America), so North American travelers move through town with zero language friction.

faq.q: Where should you stay for a honeymoon on Ambergris Caye?
faq.a: For seclusion, Cayo Espanto is a private island 3 miles off San Pedro with 7 all-inclusive villas and an 18-guest cap from ~US$1,695/villa/night; for adults-only boutique romance, Matachica offers thatched casitas. Both read romance-forward because the property caps guest count and builds the stay around couples.

faq.q: Can you fish the Grand Slam from Ambergris Caye?
faq.a: Yes — Ambergris fronts 400+ sq mi of flats, channels and lagoons where bonefish, permit and tarpon can all be landed in one day, with El Pescador the Orvis-endorsed base for 50+ years. Tarpon peaks July–September; bonefish and permit run year-round, so the slam is a realistic single-day target.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on Ambergris Caye?
faq.a: Island remoteness for serious medical events, not crime. San Pedro's Lighthouse Medical Center handles urgent care, but serious trauma routes to Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital in Belize City — the only trauma centre in Belize — then to the US, requiring air/water transfer off the island. Dengue is the primary mosquito-borne concern; there is no malaria on the cayes (Belize was WHO-certified malaria-free in 2023).

faq.q: Is diving the Great Blue Hole dangerous?
faq.a: It is an advanced dive, not a beginner novelty. The Blue Hole bottoms below recreational limits (~410 ft total); recreational dives target ~130 ft along the stalactite ledges, so treat it as advanced/technical-adjacent with sound gas planning. The offshore boat crossing is 2.5–3 hours each way, or ~20 minutes by scenic flight from San Pedro.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Aruba?
faq.a: Not storms or crime - small stuff. Aruba is south of the hurricane belt (very low storm risk) and low-crime, so plan for petty theft, strong sun and dengue, plus no-fly 18-24h if you dive the Antilla. It's about as low-stress as Caribbean travel gets.

faq.q: When is the best time to go to Aruba?
faq.a: Year-round - Aruba is warm, dry and reliably sunny with no real storm season. December-April is peak (winter escape, highest prices); May-August is warm, quieter value and windiest (best for windsurf and Hi-Winds).

faq.q: Which beach - Eagle or Palm?
faq.a: Both: Eagle Beach for the wide, quiet, top-rated sand and fofoti trees; Palm Beach for the resort strip, watersports and nightlife. Most people beach at Eagle and stay at Palm.

faq.q: Do I need to be a diver to see the Antilla wreck?
faq.a: No - the water is so clear that snorkelers can see the 400-ft wreck from the surface in ~60ft, and most excursions include boat, snorkel gear and guiding. Certified divers penetrate deeper sections (advanced); everyone else snorkels the shallows (no no-fly restriction).

faq.q: Is Aruba good for windsurfing or a wildlife day?
faq.a: Both are signatures. Hadicurari (Fisherman's Huts) is a world-class windsurf/kite beach (Hi-Winds each June/July), and you can wade with flamingos on Renaissance Island or hike Arikok National Park to the Natural Pool - beyond the beach, Aruba has real range.

faq.q: How many dives do you get on a Belize Aggressor liveaboard trip?
faq.a: Up to five dives a day — 24–27 dives on a 7-night charter, 39–42 on a 10-night. The Aggressor III/IV depart the Fort George dock in Belize City every Saturday at 6 pm, dive Sunday morning to Friday noon, and reach all three atolls, so the liveaboard converts a long day-boat run into unlimited access to Lighthouse Reef, Turneffe and Glover's.

faq.q: How deep is the Great Blue Hole dive and do you need to be certified?
faq.a: The dive reaches ~40 m/130 ft — at or beyond the recreational limit — to see the stalactites that hang between roughly 100–140 ft. Bottom time is measured in minutes and nitrogen narcosis is a real factor, so reputable operators strongly recommend or require Advanced Open Water certification. It is a deliberately deep dive, not a beginner novelty.

faq.q: What is there to do on the Belize atolls if you don't dive?
faq.a: The atoll cayes carry barefoot reef-island character for surface-interval and non-diver days. Tobacco Caye is a few-acre reef caye with snorkel-off-the-dock access; Half Moon Caye is a natural monument with ~4,000 nesting red-footed boobies and an observation tower; Long Caye is the inhabited base camp for Blue Hole and Half Moon Caye dives.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on an atoll dive trip?
faq.a: Offshore remoteness from the chamber. The only DAN-Preferred recompression chamber in Belize is on San Pedro, Ambergris Caye — hours of boat-then-air transit from a hit at Lighthouse Reef (~70 km/43 mi offshore) or Glover's. Liveaboards carry onboard O2 and run DAN protocols as first response, which is why depth and deco discipline are non-negotiable and DAN insurance with evacuation coverage is effectively mandatory.

faq.q: How long do you have to wait to fly after diving the Blue Hole?
faq.a: Plan an 18–24 hour buffer. DAN guidance sets a minimum 12-hour surface interval after a single no-deco dive and a minimum 18 hours after multi-day repetitive diving, which every liveaboard trip is; 24 hours is the recommended general practice. A 7-night Aggressor charter ends diving Friday around noon for a Saturday departure precisely to give that buffer before the BZE flight home.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Bonaire?
faq.a: Dive discipline, not danger. Because Bonaire is 24/7 drive-up shore diving, hold the no-fly 18-24h window and manage repetitive profiles. The on-island hyperbaric chamber next to the Kralendijk hospital is 24-hour and operational (2026).

faq.q: Do I have to pay the Bonaire nature fee and what does it cost?
faq.a: Yes - a mandatory US$40 STINAPA nature tag for all water activities (2026); it funds no-touch/no-anchor enforcement, fish surveys and reef restoration, and also covers Washington Slagbaai NP. Buy it online before you dive.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Bonaire?
faq.a: Year-round, but December-April is peak (cooler water, best visibility) and April-August brings the calmest seas and superb viz - Bonaire is south of the hurricane belt so there's no real storm season.

faq.q: Which Bonaire dive sites should I not miss?
faq.a: The Hilma Hooker wreck (30m), 1000 Steps (shallow, snorkel-friendly), Salt Pier (pillar ecosystems - only when no ship is in port) and a Klein Bonaire boat day; most of the ~89 sites are self-guided drive-and-dive off the yellow stones.

faq.q: Is Bonaire a liveaboard destination?
faq.a: No - Bonaire is the world's shore/drive-and-dive capital (unlimited-shore packages, drive-thru tank pickup), not a liveaboard base. Book it as a resort-and-shore dive trip, not a Dive Liveaboards sailing.

faq.q: Is Cabo Pulmo worth diving, and what will I see?
faq.a: Yes — it is arguably the Sea of Cortez's best dive, because protection worked: total fish biomass rebounded 463% by 2009 on the Gulf's only living hard-coral reef. Expect schooling jacks, groupers and rays, and in warm summer–fall water a bull-shark aggregation.

faq.q: Do I need to be certified, and can non-divers go?
faq.a: You dive within your card with a mandatory park guide (max 6 divers each), and non-divers can snorkel the same no-take reef. The rules are strict — no gloves, no touching, licensed pangas only — and enforced; break them and you can be pulled from the water.

faq.q: Can couples make a romantic escape of Cabo Pulmo?
faq.a: Only if "romantic" means off-grid and simple — there is no resort or spa layer. Lodging is solar eco-cabañas and a tiny villa cluster (~5 villas), which suits low-key couples; anyone wanting branded luxury bases in Los Cabos or the East Cape and day-trips in.

faq.q: Is diving here dangerous — what's the real risk?
faq.a: The gatekeeper is medevac distance, not the diving itself. Cabo Pulmo is off-grid with no chamber or hospital in the village; the nearest recompression chamber and trauma care are ~2–3 hours away in Los Cabos, so dive conservatively, carry DAN cover, and observe 18–24 h no-fly before an SJD departure.

faq.q: When can I dive Socorro from Cabo, and what will I see?
faq.a: Socorro runs by liveaboard only, roughly November–June, on a ~24-hour crossing from Cabo — there is no day-boat option. The draw is giant Pacific mantas that approach and stay through whole dives, up to 10 shark species, dolphins, whale sharks (Nov–Dec) and humpbacks (Jan–Mar). Book berths 6–12+ months out.

faq.q: When is whale season in Cabo?
faq.a: December 15 to April 15, with peak sightings January–March. Humpbacks breach and mate while gray whales pass with newborn calves, all on boat-based tours out of Cabo.

faq.q: When is Bisbee's, and is Cabo really the "Marlin Capital"?
faq.a: Bisbee's Black & Blue runs the third week of October — Oct 19–24 in 2026 — with a purse topping $11.5 million, and Cabo backs the "Marlin Capital" tag with year-round blue and black marlin, dorado and tuna. Tournament-week lodging and charters sell out months ahead.

faq.q: Is Cabo good for a honeymoon, and where's the top end?
faq.a: Yes — it is one of North America's densest ultra clusters, with multiple Forbes Five-Star flags. The honeymoon flagships are Las Ventanas al Paraíso (Rosewood) and One&Only Palmilla; Waldorf Astoria Pedregal, Montage and Chileno Bay sit alongside on the corridor's rare swimmable coves.

faq.q: Is diving Socorro dangerous?
faq.a: It is advanced, remote diving — manageable with discipline. Socorro has strong currents, deep pelagic sites and no chamber at the archipelago; a hit means a ~24-hour steam back to Cabo's chamber. Dive within your certification, follow the boat's conservative plan, carry DAN evacuation cover, and wait 18–24 h before flying home.

faq.q: What health risks should I actually plan for in Cancún?
faq.a: Water, mosquitoes, hurricanes and sargassum — not violent crime. Drink bottled/purified water; use repellent for dengue (no malaria in Quintana Roo tourist zones); hurricane season runs June–November with September riskiest; and sargassum peaks around July in 2026.

faq.q: Will sargassum ruin the beaches in 2026?
faq.a: It's a real risk in 2026 — plan location, don't cancel. 2026 is tracking as one of the worst sargassum years on record, often peaking around July in the Riviera Maya; north Cancún and Playa Mujeres are among the more protected stretches, and Jan–March runs lowest on sargassum.

faq.q: When and how can I swim with whale sharks?
faq.a: Mid-May to mid-September, peaking June–August, on a snorkel-only boat excursion off Isla Mujeres/Holbox — the world's largest whale-shark aggregation. It's a green-season spike inside the low-price window, so rooms are cheaper then; life-vest, no-touch, follow-the-guide.

faq.q: Can beginners dive MUSA and the reef?
faq.a: Yes — MUSA is one of the most accessible dives anywhere. The 470+ statues sit 3.5–8 m down, shallow enough for Open Water divers, snorkelers and glass-bottom boats; no-fly-after-diving is 18–24 hours and these are shallow (≤9 m) day dives.

faq.q: Is Cancún good for an all-inclusive honeymoon, and where's the top end?
faq.a: Yes — it's a honeymoon engine. The Hotel Zone is dense all-inclusive inventory; the one true ultra address in Cancún proper is NIZUC (Punta Nizuc, ~15 min from the airport), with the deepest luxury bench just down-corridor in Mayakoba/Maroma (Rosewood, Banyan Tree, Maroma/Belmond).

faq.q: How do you get around Caye Caulker — do you need a car?
faq.a: No cars at all. The ~5-mile island runs on bikes (from ~15 BZD/day) and golf carts (~125–150 BZD/day) on sand streets, reached by high-speed water taxi (~45 min from Belize City) or small plane on the Tropic Air / Maya Island Air airstrip. The whole "Go Slow" experience is walkable and bikeable in an afternoon.

faq.q: Is Caye Caulker good for snorkeling and diving?
faq.a: Yes — it is a value snorkel/dive base on the same Belize Barrier Reef as Ambergris. The Hol Chan Marine Reserve trip (US$15 park fee) puts you with sharks, rays and turtles in Belize's oldest marine park; local operators run half-days ~US$50 and full-days ~US$90, with best visibility March–June.

faq.q: Can you sail to the Blue Hole from Caye Caulker?
faq.a: Yes — the Ragga 3-day/2-night sail (~US$400, Tuesday/Friday departures) runs Caulker to Placencia via the Blue Hole and reef, camping on tiny cayes with chef-cooked lobster on deck. Day options add manatees at Swallow Caye Wildlife Sanctuary (10 BZD sanctuary fee).

faq.q: What's the food and lobster scene on Caye Caulker?
faq.a: Fry-jack breakfasts and beach BBQ anchor the everyday scene, and Lobsterfest lands in July as the island's biggest food event. Lobster season itself runs roughly mid-June to mid-February, so a summer visit catches both the festival and fresh lobster.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on Caye Caulker?
faq.a: Two things: there is no recompression chamber on Caulker (nearest is San Pedro/Ambergris, so dive-accident cases are boated across — build in transfer time and carry DAN), and The Split is not a lifeguarded beach. The channel has tidal current and boat traffic, so swim to the sides, watch for boats, and don't swim impaired at the Lazy Lizard. Hurricane risk peaks Sep–Oct.

faq.q: Is diving the Blue Hole from here dangerous?
faq.a: It is a deep dive (>100 ft) for experienced/advanced divers only — verify certification and operator briefing. Allow 18–24 hours before flying, because many guests leave BZE by puddle-jumper, and remember the nearest chamber is on Ambergris, so plan conservative profiles and factor the boat transfer time.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Cozumel?
faq.a: Decompression discipline, not crime — this is a repetitive multi-day dive island. Follow DAN's no-fly windows strictly (12h single, 18h multi-day, 24h conservative), because Cozumel's day-boat profiles stack dives fast; the island has multiple chambers, but a bad no-fly call is the classic mistake. Also plan for dengue (repellent), bottled water and hurricane season (Jun–Nov).

faq.q: Is drift diving in Cozumel dangerous?
faq.a: No, when you take the drift briefing seriously — but it is not passive. Expect a near-constant ~1.5-knot current that does the swimming for you; do a controlled descent, stay with the group and dive master, deploy an SMB, and dive within your certification. Santa Rosa Wall is expert-only; Palancar Gardens suits most certified divers.

faq.q: What are the best dive sites in Cozumel, and can beginners dive them?
faq.a: Palancar Gardens is the everyone-friendly classic — coral pinnacles, archways and swim-throughs at 100-ft-plus visibility with mild current — while Santa Rosa Wall and Columbia Deep are advanced drifts. Beginners and newly certified divers do best at Palancar; Santa Rosa, dropping from ~15 m into the blue, is expert-only.

faq.q: Can I do a liveaboard from Cozumel?
faq.a: Not from Cozumel itself — it is a day-boat island. True liveaboard-style multi-day diving goes to Banco Chinchorro, ~30–35 nm off Costa Maya, launched from Xcalak or Mahahual to the south, not Cozumel. The luxury alternative near Cozumel is a private crewed dive-yacht charter, since overnight liveaboards are effectively banned inside the national park.

faq.q: Can non-divers snorkel Cozumel, and what's the reef fee?
faq.a: Yes — the reef is superb for snorkelers, from Palancar shallows to the El Cielo starfish sandbar by catamaran. Everyone entering the marine park pays the reef bracelet, MX$220 (~US$13) per person per day as of Jan 2026; snorkel tours carry no no-fly restriction, making them a good last-day option before a flight.

faq.q: Is Cozumel good for a honeymoon or a couples' dive trip?
faq.a: Yes — it pairs world-class diving with real staffed villas. Luxury Cozumel and Villa Experience run oceanfront staffed homes (chef, concierge) from ~US$450/night, and there is no branded ultra flag on-island, so for hotel-brand luxury couples ferry to Mayakoba (Rosewood, Banyan Tree) ~an hour away.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Cozumel?
faq.a: December–March is peak, with the calmest seas, clearest skies and legendary 200-ft-plus visibility. November and May are the value sweet spots — near-peak conditions at ~25–40% (Nov) and ~20–30% (May) below Dec rates; May–September brings the warmest, calmest water (~27–28°C) but summer humidity and hurricane risk.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Curacao?
faq.a: Dive discipline, not danger. Hold the no-fly 18-24h window and manage deep profiles (the Superior Producer sits at 30m). Reassuringly, Curacao Medical Center has an on-island recompression chamber - the ABC's regional dive-emergency facility.

faq.q: Is Curacao a liveaboard destination?
faq.a: No - like its ABC neighbours it is shore + day-boat diving only (packages, private charters, PADI 5-star operators), not a liveaboard base. Book it as a resort-and-boat dive trip, not a Dive Liveaboards sailing.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit and dive Curacao?
faq.a: Year-round - Curacao is south of the hurricane belt with warm, clear water all year. December-April is the drier peak; May-November is warmer and quieter (best value), with the odd short shower.

faq.q: Which Curacao dive sites should I not miss?
faq.a: The Tugboat (5m, beginner-perfect), the Mushroom Forest + Blue Room boat run, the Superior Producer deep wreck (30m), and a Klein Curacao islet day; many west-end sites are also shore-accessible.

faq.q: Is there more to Curacao than diving?
faq.a: Yes - it's the ABC's cultural anchor: UNESCO Willemstad (Handelskade, floating market, Queen Emma pontoon bridge), the island's Jewish and slavery heritage, and Mt Christoffel to hike - a rounded island, not a single-note dive stop.

faq.q: Is the East Cape a good honeymoon base?
faq.a: Yes — it holds two of Mexico's most serious luxury resorts on one estate. Costa Palmas fronts a rare swimmable Cabo-side beach (3 km) with the Four Seasons and Amanvari, 45 minutes from SJD, so couples get calm water plus branded ultra away from the corridor crowds.

faq.q: When can I see whales in the Sea of Cortez here?
faq.a: Late December to early April, with the blue-whale peak Feb–Apr. Gray, humpback, blue and fin whales all pass offshore, on day tours or private charters out of the East Cape — one of Earth's richest whale seas.

faq.q: When is the fishing and the wind best on the East Cape?
faq.a: Two opposite seasons: billfish and dorado peak May to early November in glass-calm water, while the El Norte wind turns Los Barriles into a 15–25 kt kite and windsurf arena Dec–March. Pick the season for the sport you came for.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Fernando de Noronha?
faq.a: August–November is the dive peak because the dry season delivers the clearest water and calmest seas, with the September–October visibility apex reaching up to ~50 m. April–June (rainy) is the diver's value window — rain hits the surface, not the reef, so visibility stays strong and the island is quieter.

faq.q: How do you get to Baía do Sancho?
faq.a: Baía do Sancho is reached only by boat or by a staircase carved into the volcanic rock face, and a marine-park pass is required. It has been voted the best beach in the world by TripAdvisor travelers five times, which is why access is deliberately controlled.

faq.q: Which is the best honeymoon pousada on Fernando de Noronha?
faq.a: Pousada Maravilha is consistently ranked the island's top honeymoon hotel, with six sea-facing apartments plus bungalows with private hot tubs, an infinity pool, fine dining and a spa. Nannai Noronha (10 bungalows, private verandas, direct beach access) is the other ultra-tier couples pick.

faq.q: Can you swim with the spinner dolphins at Baía dos Golfinhos?
faq.a: No — Baía dos Golfinhos is a no-entry protected dolphin resting bay: no descending, no swimming, no boats inside. Spinner dolphins are watched from a clifftop viewpoint, best at first light. This is a legal protection, not a suggestion.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Remoteness and medical evacuation. Fernando de Noronha has a hyperbaric chamber adjacent to Hospital São Lucas, but the hospital provides basic emergency care only — serious trauma or complex decompression illness requires evacuation to the mainland (Recife/Natal), and weather can delay the flight. Carry insurance with medevac and dive conservatively.

faq.q: Is diving the Corveta Ipiranga wreck dangerous?
faq.a: It is technical / Extended-Range diving: the wreck sits at ~62 m off Ponta da Sapata, so operators require Nitrox plus ~50 logged dives and evaluation dives before permitting it, always with a pro. Recreational divers stay on shallower 8–22 m reef and cave sites. Because you leave only by air, observe an 18–24 h surface interval before your flight.

faq.q: How dangerous is diving Darwin and Wolf — can beginners do it?
faq.a: No — these are advanced dives, not a beginner destination. Reputable operators gate Darwin/Wolf on Advanced Open Water certification plus logged current/cold-water experience: divers hook onto ledges in ripping current at 20–30 m in 16–24 °C water, far from support. Gordon Rocks and Kicker Rock are the intermediate-to-advanced warm-ups.

faq.q: How long should I wait to fly after diving the Galápagos?
faq.a: Plan a full 18–24 hours before the island-to-mainland flight. A liveaboard week is repetitive multi-day diving (DAN: 18 h minimum, 24 h recommended), and Quito sits at ~2,850 m — so never book a same-day-as-last-dive flight. The only hyperbaric chamber is in Puerto Ayora, hours by boat from Darwin/Wolf, so DAN evacuation insurance is effectively mandatory.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive for hammerheads and whale sharks?
faq.a: June–November — the cool, plankton-rich season — is the big-animal window, with whale sharks peaking August–September, because the Humboldt upwelling drops water to 16–24 °C and concentrates pelagic life; ~90% of monitored hammerheads stay in the reserve then, schooling in the hundreds. Expect cooler water and stronger current.

faq.q: Do I need a cruise, or can I stay on land?
faq.a: Both work, but the iconic sites need a boat. Darwin and Wolf are liveaboard-only, and by park rule every visitor-site landing must be led by a licensed naturalist guide. Land-based island-hopping (Santa Cruz, Isabela) covers tortoises, Tortuga Bay and day dives; the deep wildlife (Española albatross, Genovesa seabirds) needs an expedition cruise.

faq.q: What's the best Galápagos trip for a honeymoon?
faq.a: A small all-suite expedition yacht or the highlands Pikaia Lodge. The warm season (Dec–May, water 25–27 °C, calm seas) is the easiest for first-timers and snorkeling; book 6–12 months ahead because the top cabins and suites — and holiday sailings — sell out first.

faq.q: Which Guanacaste beaches are best for calm swimming?
faq.a: Playa Hermosa and Playas del Coco anchor the calm-water belt. Blue Flag Playa Hermosa is quiet and low-key, and lively Playas del Coco — the region's oldest beach town, 30 minutes from LIR — is the dive, fishing and water-sports hub; both are amenity-rich swim beaches away from the open surf.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book a Guanacaste destination wedding?
faq.a: Book 12–18 months out for the most in-demand properties. Peak-season wedding dates at the top Guanacaste resorts fill 12–18 months in advance, and booking early also locks the best group room-block pricing before rates compress; plan 9–12 months minimum.

faq.q: Can you surf Witch's Rock and Ollie's Point from Tamarindo?
faq.a: Yes — both are boat-access breaks. Roca Bruja (Witch's Rock) inside Santa Rosa National Park is a world-class sand-bottom beach break and Ollie's Point is one of Costa Rica's best right-hand point breaks, reached on 1–2-hour open-water boat runs from Tamarindo, Coco or Flamingo.

faq.q: When can you dive with bull sharks at the Bat Islands?
faq.a: June through October is the window. The Bat Islands "Big Scare" is the only bull-shark dive in Costa Rica, where advanced divers descend with bull sharks up to 3+ metres; reliability peaks June–October and it runs as an advanced-cert charter out of Playas del Coco / Flamingo — a wildlife dive, not a guarantee.

faq.q: When is leatherback turtle nesting season at Playa Grande?
faq.a: Late October to mid-February, peaking December–January. Playa Grande / Las Baulas is the second-largest Pacific leatherback nesting beach on earth; ranger-led night tours run in that window with a 15-per-group cap for roughly $25 including entry and guide.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Pacific rip currents are the primary beach hazard. Guanacaste's open Pacific beaches carry rip currents and Tamarindo's surf adds board/reef injury risk, so swim at guarded or calm beaches like Conchal and Hermosa and take beginner surf only with a certified instructor.

faq.q: Is Bat Islands diving dangerous?
faq.a: It's advanced-only, not for new divers. The "Big Scare" requires a minimum PADI Advanced Open Water certification — strong shifting currents, thermoclines and 30 m+ depths — so enforce no-fly-after-diving (18 h single / 24 h repetitive) before any LIR/SJO flight and carry DAN cover.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in the water?
faq.a: Riptides on the open beaches, not the sheltered bays. The horseshoe coves (La Entrega, Maguey, San Agustín) are genuinely calm and swimmable, but open stretches of Tangolunda and Chahué carry rip currents — swim only the flagged, sheltered coves, and heed the flags.

faq.q: Which bays are calm enough for swimming and families?
faq.a: The horseshoe coves. La Entrega is the best land-accessible snorkel cove — the reef starts feet from shore — and Maguey, Órgano and San Agustín stay calm inside their coves; that's the difference from surf-driven Puerto Escondido up the coast.

faq.q: What's the one must-do day here?
faq.a: The nine-bays boat tour — a full-day (~7 h) expedition across the nine bays with beach and snorkel stops, bookable through Amstar's "Sea and Sun"/"Seven Bays" excursions or affiliate marketplaces (the National Park conservation bracelet is a cash pass-through).

faq.q: When can I see whales?
faq.a: Humpbacks run **Dec 15–Mar 21**, with sightings on **over 97% of tours** at the peak, on boat safaris out of Santa Cruz; dolphins and turtles are year-round, and turtle nesting (olive-ridley/green) runs Jul–Jan.

faq.q: Can beginners dive the reef here?
faq.a: Yes — the protected Pacific reef is beginner-friendly. La Entrega runs 10–12 m and San Agustín adds a ~30 m sunken ship for advanced divers, with up to ~18 m visibility in the dry season; book only PADI-certified operators (Huatulco Dive Center, Anfibios, Hurricane Divers).

faq.q: Is there culture beyond the beach?
faq.a: Yes — Copalita is one of only two seaside archaeological sites in Mexico (with Tulum), a Zapotec/Mixtec city settled by ~500 BC in rainforest above the river mouth, and La Crucecita's zócalo holds one of Mexico's largest Guadalupe ceiling murals.

faq.q: Is Huatulco good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, for calm-bay romance rather than branded-ultra. Secrets Huatulco is the adults-only, all-oceanfront-suite anchor of the Tangolunda strip; the coast tops out at premier all-inclusive plus a top oceanfront villa in Conejos — there is no Aman/Rosewood-tier hotel here.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on Isla Mujeres?
faq.a: Water, weather and currents — not crime. Drink bottled water, use repellent for dengue (no malaria in the tourist zone), and note hurricane season runs June–November with September riskiest. Playa Norte is comparatively sargassum-protected, but 2026 is heavy region-wide; the Punta Sur loggerhead dives sit in strong currents, so they are for advanced divers only.

faq.q: Is swimming with whale sharks or diving Punta Sur dangerous?
faq.a: The whale-shark encounter is snorkel-only with no decompression restriction — wear the vest, no touching, stay with the guide against boat traffic and open-water current. Punta Sur's summer loggerhead dive is a strong-current drift for advanced divers with a local guide; observe no-fly of 18–24 hours after any scuba.

faq.q: When and how can I swim with whale sharks from Isla Mujeres?
faq.a: Roughly June to September, on a snorkel-only boat excursion to the aggregation — the island is the whale-shark snorkel capital of the region. Tours book about 30–39 days out on average and sell out fast in peak summer, so reserve at least 3–6 weeks ahead; it is snorkel-only, with no scuba allowed.

faq.q: Can beginners dive MUSA from Isla Mujeres?
faq.a: Yes — MUSA is one of the most accessible dives anywhere. Its 470+ statues sit just 3.5–8 m down, shallow enough for Open Water divers and snorkelers, and at ≤9 m these are easy day dives. Advanced divers can add the Punta Sur loggerhead drift in summer, which sits in strong current and is guided-only.

faq.q: Is Playa Norte good, and will sargassum ruin it?
faq.a: It is the island's signature beach — waist-deep, glass-calm turquoise you can wade out a hundred meters into — and one of the most sargassum-protected stretches in the region. In a heavy year like 2026 that protection is a genuine edge, but still disclose: no beach is fully immune, and mornings are cleanest.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for Komodo, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Indonesia at Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution (reissued 30 April 2025). Its only Level 4 (Do Not Travel) carve-outs are Central Papua (Papua Tengah) and Highland Papua (Papua Pegunungan), for civil unrest; Komodo, in East Nusa Tenggara, sits well apart from both. The material regional flag comes from the UK FCDO, which advises against all travel within 7 km of the crater of Mount Lewotobi Laki-Laki on Flores - a volcano that erupted on 17 June 2025, holds Indonesia's highest alert (level 4), and carries mud/debris-flow warnings plus disruption to flights to and from Bali and Flores. Because Labuan Bajo, Komodo's gateway, is on Flores, build slack into flight connections and confirm status before travel. Carry DAN membership plus separate dive-accident insurance and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Since 13 October 2018 Komodo's gateway has had its own chamber: a hyperbaric oxygen chamber at Siloam Hospitals Labuan Bajo (Flores), the first in East Nusa Tenggara and an eight-patient chamber, so divers no longer have to be flown to Bali first. The fallback remains Sanglah General Hospital in Denpasar, Bali, roughly 1.5 hours by air. Confirm the Labuan Bajo chamber's 24-hour readiness on your dates with the operator or DAN, and note that the Mount Lewotobi flight disruption can affect the Bali evacuation leg. Komodo's currents put a premium on conservative profiles and dive-accident insurance.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Komodo?
faq.a: May-October, the Southeast Monsoon dry season, is the popular liveaboard window, with northern waters at 30C and optimal visibility. The cooler southern sites (Manta Alley area) carry more nutrient and colder water; route and month are set by the operator's north/south plan.

faq.q: Where do I see mantas in Komodo?
faq.a: Manta Alley and Manta Point are the named manta sites - cleaning stations and feeding aggregations in current.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Castle Rock and Crystal Rock are high-current pinnacle dives suited to experienced divers with reef hooks; sheltered sites and the Sangeang volcanic slopes suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards. Dive within your certification and the briefing.

faq.q: Can I see the Komodo dragons on the same trip?
faq.a: Yes - Komodo National Park pairs the diving with ranger-guided dragon walks on Komodo and Rinca and the Padar viewpoint; most liveaboards include a park day.

faq.q: How far ahead do Komodo liveaboards book?
faq.a: Peak dry-season (May-October) weeks on preferred vessels fill earliest; hold roughly 3-9 months out for peak windows, nearer term for the shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

faq.q: When and how can I swim with whale sharks in La Paz?
faq.a: October 1 to April 30, on a licensed half-day snorkel in the bay's protected refuge zone — never scuba. Encounters are capped at 5 swimmers plus a certified guide per shark for 30 minutes, with no touching, to protect the juveniles that feed there.

faq.q: Is La Paz a good island and beach base?
faq.a: Yes — it is the launch port for the whole Sea-of-Cortez set: protected Balandra, Tecolote, the Malecón waterfront and boat trips to UNESCO-listed Espíritu Santo. It's the quiet, low-key alternative to the Los Cabos corridor two hours south.

faq.q: What is there to dive around La Paz?
faq.a: The signature dive is the Salvatierra, a 1976 ferry wreck at 18–20 m that's now a thriving artificial reef, diveable near year-round, plus the El Bajo seamount. La Paz has its own recompression chamber (confirm status at booking) and DAN emergency is +1-919-684-9111.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Missing the season, not crime. Whale sharks are gone May–Sep, sea lions close Jun 1–Aug 31, both are snorkel-only (no touch, no scuba), and hurricane season runs Jun–Nov. Book the Oct–Apr window ahead and carry trip insurance for summer/fall.

faq.q: When is the best time to see blue whales in Loreto?
faq.a: Roughly January–March, strongest early February to about mid-March, because that's when blue whales feed in the bay; gray and humpback come slightly earlier. Tours are 4–6-hour pangas from Loreto Marina or Puerto Escondido — book the short window 3–6 months ahead.

faq.q: What are Loreto's islands like?
faq.a: Five uninhabited islands — Coronado, del Carmen, Danzante, Monserrat and Santa Catalina — shelter the bay with turquoise coves, white-sand beaches and a sea-lion colony, all inside a protected marine park with 40+ snorkel/dive sites. Isla Coronado is the classic day trip.

faq.q: Is Loreto good for a golf-and-spa couples escape?
faq.a: Yes, if you want premier rather than ultra. Villa del Palmar at Danzante Bay has Mexico's only TPC course (Best Golf Course in Mexico 2020) and a 39,000-sq-ft spa on a secluded bay — position it as a premier golf-and-whale escape, not an Aman-tier ultra.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for — is the diving remote?
faq.a: Yes — chamber distance is the gatekeeper. Loreto has local clinics for routine care, but a serious dive bend routes ~350 km south to the La Paz chamber (or Los Cabos), so dive conservatively, keep whale-panga trips to licensed no-chase operators, and observe 18–24 h no-fly before the LTO departure.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for diving Mahahual?
faq.a: Remote medevac - the load-bearing risk. Mahahual has NO hyperbaric chamber; the nearest DAN-certified chamber is in Cozumel, a multi-hour transit from a Chinchorro site ~25 miles offshore. Dive conservatively, hold no-fly 18-24h, and treat DCS as a logistics problem.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Mahahual and Chinchorro?
faq.a: May-September - the counterintuitive answer: calmest seas, best visibility (~15-30m) and the crocodile season (Jun 1-Sep 30), even though it overlaps the rainy/hurricane months. Winter (Nov-Mar) sees more wind and Chinchorro is often blown out.

faq.q: Can I day-dive Banco Chinchorro, and how?
faq.a: Yes - most Mahahual/Xcalak operators run day-trips for certified divers: a 2-tank ($275) or 3-tank ($325) day with a Cayo Centro stop, an 80-90-minute crossing each way. The operator handles the limited federal permit when you book; May-September has the calmest seas.

faq.q: Can you really swim with wild crocodiles at Chinchorro?
faq.a: Yes - it's the only legally permitted in-water wild-crocodile encounter on Earth, and only XTC Dive Center holds the federal permit. The season is a hard window of June 1 to September 30, capped at 6 people (2 in the water with the handler at a time), flotation device required. Book far ahead.

faq.q: What is the Banco Chinchorro liveaboard experience actually like?
faq.a: It's a stilt-hut expedition, not a cruise ship. Multi-day trips overnight in a palafito on Cayo Centro - a basic 2x2m stilt-deck fishing hut with hammocks and no services - legalized in 2010. It's the closest access to the remote walls and ~200 wrecks; permit-scarce, so book the specialist operator well ahead.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for the Maldives, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places the Maldives at Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution, due to terrorism, with no sub-national carve-out (accessed 2026-08-09). State adds that attacks may occur on remote islands, which can lengthen the response time of authorities - worth weighing on a liveaboard far from Male. The UK FCDO advises against no travel but says terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out and could be indiscriminate; the stricter baseline (State Level 2) sets the posture. Carry DAN membership plus separate dive-accident insurance (liveaboard.com requires divers to independently hold it) and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Master Liveaboards' Maldives FAQ names five operational recompression chambers, with the largest and longest-operating on Bandos Island in North Male Atoll, 15 minutes by speedboat from Male - the closest to a Male departure. Others sit at Kuramathi (North Ari), Kuredu (Lhaviyani, the only chamber in the northern Maldives, with a clinic reporting operators on call 24 hours), Kandima (Dhaalu) and ADK Hospital in Male. Recompression treatment is likely to involve evacuation by private speedboat or seaplane, so confirm the chamber nearest your route and its readiness on your dates with the operator or DAN.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive the Maldives?
faq.a: December-May is the dry northeast-monsoon window - calmer seas, clearer water (15-20 m+), best for channel pelagics. June-November is the southwest monsoon: greener water but the manta and whale-shark season. Water stays 26-29C year-round.

faq.q: When and where do I see mantas and whale sharks?
faq.a: June-October in the southwest monsoon, with Hanifaru Bay in Baa Atoll the signature aggregation site (snorkel-only in the protected core); South Ari Atoll holds whale sharks year-round.

faq.q: Which atolls does a liveaboard week cover?
faq.a: Central-atoll routes work North/South Male, Ari, Vaavu and Baa; southern and specialist routes reach Fuvahmulah (tiger and thresher sharks) and Huvadhoo. Route choice tracks the monsoon - central-atoll clear-water weeks in the northeast season, manta routes in the southwest.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Channel (kandu) dives are current-driven drift dives suited to experienced divers; thila pinnacles and lagoon sites suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards for the multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Maldives liveaboards book?
faq.a: Northeast-season (Dec-Apr) clear-water weeks and manta-season (Jun-Oct) berths on preferred vessels fill earliest; hold roughly 3-9 months out for peak windows, nearer term for shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

faq.q: Do you need a guide to hike Corcovado National Park?
faq.a: Yes — a certified guide is legally mandatory for all Corcovado entry, a SINAC rule in force since February 1, 2014 and enforced at every ranger station, where unguided visitors are turned away. Build the guided-trek product; there is no compliant self-guided version to sell.

faq.q: Can you dive Cocos Island on a day trip?
faq.a: No. Cocos is liveaboard-only — it lies ~342 mi off the Pacific coast, an ~36-hr open-ocean crossing from Puntarenas, and is sold as 8/10/12-night charters (15/21/27 dives) via Aggressor or Undersea Hunter. Berths book 6–18 months out, so plan far ahead.

faq.q: Are the Osa eco-lodges right for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — the Osa is honeymoon-grade seclusion without the resort cliché: private-reserve bungalows over the Pacific, canopy suites and no Wi-Fi. Lapa Rios alone offers 16 ocean-view bungalows across 1,000 protected acres, and remote lodges bundle meals, guided excursions and transfers by necessity.

faq.q: When can you see whales in Golfo Dulce?
faq.a: Golfo Dulce — one of only four tropical fjords on Earth — draws both hemispheres' humpbacks, so the season is unusually long: Southern-hemisphere humpbacks calve July–November (prime late Aug–Sept), and Northern-hemisphere humpbacks arrive November–February.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for on a Corcovado trek?
faq.a: The tide-timed river crossings. Rio Sirena and Rio Claro are the most dangerous, with American crocodiles and bull sharks patrolling the river mouths, so guides cross only at low tide and never in storms. This — plus jungle heat and deep-remote medevac — is the true gatekeeper, above petty crime.

faq.q: Is diving Cocos Island dangerous?
faq.a: It is advanced diving in a strong-current, deeply remote environment. DAN membership and dive insurance are essential, no-fly-after-diving surface intervals apply, and because the site is ~36 hr from land the vessel itself is the only evacuation. Not a first-timer's trip.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for Palau, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Palau at Level 1 - Exercise Normal Precautions, and the UK FCDO issues no advice against travel, describing crime levels as low. Both note practical hazards rather than restrictions: unexploded WWII ordnance (found mainly on Peleliu - stay on marked paths and do not touch ordnance), diving hazards, and tropical cyclones, with an overnight curfew in Koror. The two governments agree on a Level 1 posture. Carry DAN membership plus dive-accident insurance with strong evacuation cover - the Palau Siren operator stresses that insurance covering emergency evacuation, chamber treatment and medical costs is a must - and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Palau has one hyperbaric facility for divers - a recompression chamber at Belau National Hospital in Koror. Hospital sources describe it as operational in 2026 with a trained barotrauma team, but availability can vary, so confirm its status with your dive operator or DAN before the trip. Because the archipelago is dispersed, serious cases can require evacuation by speedboat from the vessel and, in some cases, onward air evacuation to Manila - which is why evacuation-grade dive insurance matters here.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Palau, and when do the mantas aggregate?
faq.a: The peak liveaboard season is November through May, with warm water (28-30C) year-round. For mantas at German Channel, the winter months are best - January and February can bring dozens of mantas to the cleaning station.

faq.q: Which sites define a Palau liveaboard week?
faq.a: Blue Corner (the reef-hook shark drift), German Channel (mantas), Ulong Channel (a drift past giant clams and lettuce coral), the Blue Holes cavern, the Peleliu walls, Siaes Tunnel and New Drop-Off - plus the snorkel-only Jellyfish Lake as a non-dive highlight.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Blue Corner, Peleliu Express and the channel dives are strong-current drift dives where a reef hook and good buoyancy are essential, best suited to experienced divers; sheltered reefs, Chandelier Cave and the lake suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards for the multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the operator briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Palau liveaboards book?
faq.a: The November-May peak on the marquee vessels fills earliest, with the January-February manta weeks in most demand; hold roughly 6-12 months out for peak windows and preferred boats, nearer term for the shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

name: Placencia
line: Whale sharks and mainland sand

key_facts: Placencia is Belize's southern beach peninsula with the country's best mainland beaches and its main resort/romance-wedding coast.
Gladden Spit, off Placencia, is the world's most predictable whale-shark aggregation, timed to the Mar-Jun full moons (peak Apr-May).
The southern barrier reef (Silk Cayes, Laughing Bird Caye NP, South Water Caye) launches from Placencia; the outer atolls are reachable.
Monkey River (howler monkeys, manatees) and the Cockscomb Basin (world's first jaguar preserve) are easy day trips.
Access is BZE -> PLJ (Placencia airstrip) by 20-30 min puddle-jumper on Tropic Air / Maya Island Air; ~3.5-4 hr drive alternative.

faq.q: Is Placencia good for a honeymoon or wedding?
faq.a: Yes — it is Belize's most credible mainland resort/romance market, with real luxury-to-ultra range. Naïa Resort & Spa (39 beach houses + treetop villas on 224 private acres, mile of beach, from ~US$380/night) and SLH-member Itz'ana anchor the beachfront, plus true private-island elopements offshore. The peninsula earns both the wedding and the dive log.

faq.q: When can you swim with whale sharks in Placencia?
faq.a: Around the Mar–Jun full moons at Gladden Spit — the one place on the planet where whale-shark arrival is "reasonably predictable." 2026 full moons are Mar 14, Apr 13, May 12 and Jun 11, with windows ~2 days before to ~10 days after; April and May fill first, so serious divers book three to four months ahead. Encounters are not guaranteed — you're buying the window.

faq.q: What wildlife can you see near Placencia?
faq.a: Two flagship day trips. The Monkey River eco-tour (a ~45-min coastal boat run then a river cruise) carries you into black-howler-monkey habitat with crocodiles, iguanas, toucans and manatees on the return; and the Cockscomb Basin — the world's first jaguar preserve, 128,000 acres, est. 1986 — is a half-day inland via Maya Center.

faq.q: Does Placencia have good beaches and reef?
faq.a: Yes — the country's best mainland beaches on a 16-mile peninsula, plus the closest mainland launch to the southern reef. Splash Dive Center's home waters — the Silk Cayes, South Water Caye and Laughing Bird Caye — are "postcard perfect islands on the barrier reef" with turtles, sharks, rays and eels, most a 30–60 minute run out.

faq.q: Can you fly-fish the flats in Placencia?
faq.a: Yes — the southern flats and river mouths are world-class permit water, fishable year-round for permit, bonefish and tarpon by skiff. It's a high-value niche booked through Placencia fishing lodges and guides, and a reliable green-season lever when the reef days are between fronts.

faq.q: Is there a destination spa / wellness stay in Placencia?
faq.a: Yes — Naïa Resort & Spa is built for it: a 224-acre private property with a mile of beach, a destination spa and a private-island couples retreat, strong on both romance and wellness. It's the anchor for a quiet-beach reset paired with reef or river days.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Placencia?
faq.a: Dive-chamber distance and open-water boat runs, not crime. The nearest recompression chamber is on Ambergris Caye (San Pedro), a meaningful distance north of the southern reef, so plan conservative profiles and no-fly windows; the run to Gladden Spit is ~90 minutes each way with early 6–7am departures. There is no full trauma center on the peninsula — serious cases evacuate to Belize City.

faq.q: Is swimming with whale sharks dangerous?
faq.a: It runs guided-only with a permitted operator — Gladden Spit is inside a marine reserve and only permitted operators may run the aggregation, no-touch and no-chase. Snorkelers work the surface aggregation over 2–3 hours (moderate swimming ability needed); divers descend to ~50–80 ft to meet the sharks and must be certified and guided.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Playa del Carmen?
faq.a: Sargassum, weather and water — not violent crime against tourists. 2026 is a record-forecast sargassum year, but Playa is moderate risk thanks to active municipal cleanup and a 5-km double-barrier program, with landings in pulses. Drink bottled water, use repellent for dengue (peak May–Nov, no malaria), and note hurricane season runs June–November.

faq.q: Can I dive Cozumel and the cenotes from Playa del Carmen?
faq.a: Yes — Playa is the best mainland dive base for both. Cozumel's drift-wall reef (Palancar, Santa Rosa, Columbia) is a 40-minute ferry away at ~US$32 round trip, and cenote cavern dives sit under 30 minutes inland. Cozumel walls are drift dives for a reputable operator; cenotes are guide-required and weather-independent.

faq.q: What is there to do on Fifth Avenue?
faq.a: Fifth Avenue (Quinta Avenida) is the Riviera Maya's densest dining and nightlife strip — a multi-kilometre pedestrian street of tacos-to-rooftop bars parallel to the sand. It is the town's social spine, best on a weekday evening before the crowds; guided food-and-rooftop crawls are the easy way to graze it.

faq.q: Are the Xcaret and Xplor parks worth it, especially for families?
faq.a: Yes — they are the region's marquee eco-parks. Xcaret runs cenotes, underground rivers and Maya performances; Xplor has Mexico's largest zipline circuit (14 lines over 3.8 km) plus amphibious buggies. Park admission (~US$85–110 at Xcaret) is pass-through, and both sit just outside town — a full family day out.

faq.q: Can I visit Maya ruins from Playa del Carmen?
faq.a: Yes — it is the corridor's best ruins base. Tulum's cliff-top ruins and Cobá's bikeable jungle pyramids pair in one day loop, and Chichén Itzá is a longer day trip; early morning (Nov/Feb) is best. Amstar and other DMCs run guided excursions, with ruin entry as a pass-through cost.

faq.q: Where's the best luxury for a honeymoon near Playa del Carmen?
faq.a: The Mayakoba estate and La Casa de la Playa. Mayakoba (Rosewood, Banyan Tree, Andaz) is a gated 595-acre lagoon estate of Virtuoso-affiliated flagships; La Casa de la Playa (Grupo Xcaret) is a 63-suite AAA Five-Diamond boutique ranked #1 Resort in Mexico for 2025. Both are ultra-tier honeymoon addresses on Playa's doorstep.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Playa del Carmen?
faq.a: November–March is the dry, cooler high season (best weather, highest rates); May–October is hot, humid and rainy at the cheapest rates. The value sweet spots are the May–June and November shoulders at ~30–40% off, with November landing clear of sargassum and ahead of the holiday surge.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Puerto Aventuras?
faq.a: Water, mosquitoes, hurricanes and sargassum — not crime. Drink bottled/purified water, use repellent for dengue (peak May–November, no malaria in tourist Quintana Roo), and note hurricane season runs June–November. Sargassum is heavy region-wide in 2026 (Apr–Aug), but the marina and dive focus soften the beach hit here.

faq.q: What is the marina and sportfishing like in Puerto Aventuras?
faq.a: It is one of the few mainland deep-water marinas between Cancún and Belize City — a secure safe-haven harbor for yachts, sailors and sportfishers. Offshore charters run year-round (weather permitting), with the peak billfish and mahi window in the Mar–Jun spring dry season; berth fees are pass-through and the guided charter is the commissionable wrapper.

faq.q: Is Puerto Aventuras a good dive base?
faq.a: Yes — it is a genuine near-shore reef and cenote base. The reef is only ~100 feet from the beach, so you can log several dives a day with minimal boat transit, and Cenote Azul (between Puerto Aventuras and Playa del Carmen) puts cave country within easy reach. Best reef visibility runs Nov–May.

faq.q: Is Puerto Aventuras good for families?
faq.a: Very — it is built for calm, safe family days. The adjacent Dolphin Discovery center offers sea-inlet swims with bottlenose dolphins, sea lions and manatees; add the gated 24/7-security layout, a calm marina promenade and near-shore reef, and it suits families and multigenerational groups well.

faq.q: Is Puerto Aventuras good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes, for couples who want secure and quiet over party energy. The in-community options are the branded all-inclusive Dreams Aventuras and private gated marina/golf villas with chef and concierge; the wider luxury tier runs ~US$400–600+/night in March. For branded ultra, Mayakoba (Rosewood, Banyan Tree) is ~30–40 min north with an easy marina/dive day trip.

faq.q: Can I do Maya ruins from Puerto Aventuras?
faq.a: Yes — Tulum and Cobá are easy guided day trips, alongside Akumal's turtle bay ~10 min south. Amstar and other Riviera Maya DMCs run cenote, Tulum-ruins and Akumal-turtle excursions from Puerto Aventuras; entries are pass-through, with the guided excursion the commissionable wrapper.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Puerto Aventuras?
faq.a: December–April is peak (best weather, highest rates); the value windows are the May–June and November shoulders at ~30–40% off, with November clear of sargassum. The green season (Jun–mid-Oct) is hot, rainy and cheapest with hurricane exposure — but the marina and dive product hold up better than a pure beach stay.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Puerto Morelos?
faq.a: Sargassum, hurricanes and water — not crime. 2026 is heavy region-wide for sargassum, and Puerto Morelos' open Caribbean-facing beaches are affected, so plan cenote and reef days as hedges; drink bottled water, use repellent for dengue (no malaria in the tourist zone), and note hurricane season runs June–November, September riskiest.

faq.q: Is Puerto Morelos good for diving and the Juan Escutia wreck?
faq.a: Yes — it is an underrated day-boat dive base. The Puerto Morelos Reef National Park sits under 500 m offshore, one of the Caribbean's best-preserved reefs, and the sunken Juan Escutia is now an artificial reef and fish refuge steps away. Visibility is best in the dry Oct–March window; book in town, where it is cheaper and supports local operators.

faq.q: Can I go deep-sea fishing from Puerto Morelos?
faq.a: Yes — it is a working fishing port, so charters are authentic and close at hand. Half- and full-day trips target dorado (mahi-mahi), wahoo, tuna and barracuda, with gear and guide included; the species mix is seasonal, so confirm with the operator. It pairs naturally with the fresh-off-the-boat ceviche at the beachfront cantinas.

faq.q: What is the Route of the Cenotes?
faq.a: A ~17 km jungle road of cenotes running inland from town — Puerto Morelos is its northern gateway. It strings together open, semi-open and cave cenotes for swimming, cavern diving and ziplining, at roughly 150–250 MXN entry each. Because they are shaded jungle sites, cenotes are weather-resilient — a strong rainy-day and green-season option.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Punta Cana?
faq.a: Small stuff, not violent crime: pickpocketing/theft, unlicensed excursion operators, beach rip currents and strong sun. Malaria is low but present in La Altagracia (mosquito precautions), and hurricane season is Jun-Nov (peak Aug-Oct) - carry travel insurance for a green-season trip.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Punta Cana?
faq.a: December-April is the dry, reliable peak (best weather, highest prices); March-May is the sweet spot for thinner crowds and deals; July-October is cheapest but overlaps hurricane season, so watch forecasts.

faq.q: What currency do I need in Punta Cana, and what about entry?
faq.a: The Dominican peso (DOP, ~58/USD) is official, but US dollars are accepted almost everywhere at resorts - carry small DOP for tips. Entry needs a valid passport, no visa (30 days), the $10 tourist card bundled in your airfare, and a mandatory E-Ticket before you fly.

faq.q: Is the Isla Saona day trip worth it?
faq.a: Yes - it's the most popular excursion: a catamaran and speedboat day to a national-park island of shallow natural pools and white sand, with the turtle-conservation village of Mano Juan. It sells out in peak, so book ahead through a licensed operator.

faq.q: Is Punta Cana only all-inclusive resorts, and how many days do I need?
faq.a: The resorts are the core (5-7 nights is typical), but the East rewards getting out: Saona, Hoyo Azul/Scape Park, ATV + Macao horseback, catamaran snorkel and championship golf. Budget a couple of excursion days beyond the beach.

faq.q: What exactly is the danger in the Quirimbas?
faq.a: An active ISIS-linked insurgency (ASWJ). Armed groups have attacked villages and occupied islands in the archipelago and the mainland port of Mocimboa da Praia; foreigners have been kidnapped, and the 2021 Palma attack killed or displaced thousands. Marine and health hazards are secondary to the conflict.

faq.q: Could I go with a private security arrangement or a waiver?
faq.a: No - TravelWell offers no waiver and no book path for a Level 4 zone. Evacuation from a remote island in an active-conflict setting is not assured, and even the gateway city of Pemba is high-risk. The responsible answer is to wait for the advisory to change.

faq.q: Is the rest of Mozambique off-limits too?
faq.a: No - this hold is Cabo Delgado-specific. Southern Mozambique (Maputo, Tofo, Vilanculos, the Bazaruto Archipelago, Inhambane) is far from the conflict and remains a bookable Indian-Ocean destination; that is where we point Mozambique demand today.

faq.q: When the advisory clears, what would the Quirimbas offer?
faq.a: Elite diving (Neptune's Arm and untouched reefs), humpback whales and whale sharks in season, the Swahili stone town of Ibo, and barefoot-luxury private islands (Medjumbe, Vamizi) - a world-class dive-and-heritage archipelago. All of it is held until the advisory lifts.

faq.q: What are the non-security health risks to know?
faq.a: Malaria is HIGH (prophylaxis + bite prevention essential), cyclone season is Dec-Apr, yellow-fever proof is needed only if arriving from an endemic country, and in-conflict medical/evacuation capacity is minimal - reinforcing the booking hold.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for Raja Ampat, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Indonesia at Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution (reissued 30 April 2025). Its only Level 4 (Do Not Travel) carve-outs are Central Papua (Papua Tengah) and Highland Papua (Papua Pegunungan); Raja Ampat sits in Southwest Papua (Papua Barat Daya), outside both, at the country caution baseline. The UK FCDO issues no formal advise-against level for Papua but notes armed separatist violence mainly in Highland and Central Papua, calls that security picture unpredictable, and says to take local advice; it does not name Raja Ampat. The stricter reading - the State Level 2 baseline plus the broader Papua-context caveat - sets the posture. One live note: Wayag Island and the Manyaifun/Batangpele area were reported temporarily closed to visitors over local nickel-mining disputes, so confirm current access for northern itineraries. Carry DAN membership plus dive-accident insurance with strong evacuation cover, and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: The nearest recompression chamber is in Waisai, the regency capital on Waigeo, roughly 2-4 hours from the dive sites. Its readiness cannot be assumed: dive-medicine sources warn there is no reliably operational chamber in Papua, and a DAN-documented case describes the Waisai chamber being under repair with the diver evacuated to Bali - nearly 2,000 km and around seven hours' flying (about four hours to Sorong, three more to Bali); Manado in North Sulawesi is the other referral. Treat Waisai as the nearest option, confirm its status through the operator or DAN, and carry evacuation insurance that will actually move you. Conservative profiles and nitrox matter more here than almost anywhere.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Raja Ampat?
faq.a: The main liveaboard window is roughly October-April, when seas are calmer and visibility is at its clearest; June-July brings the most unpredictable conditions and is best avoided, and several boats reposition to Komodo for the Southeast-monsoon dry season. Water stays around 28-30C year-round.

faq.q: Where do I see mantas, and what is the marquee dive?
faq.a: Manta Sandy in the Dampier Strait and Magic Mountain (Shadow Reef) in Misool are the two manta cleaning stations - reef mantas through much of the year and oceanic mantas in season at Magic Mountain. The marquee reef dive is Cape Kri, which holds a record for the most fish species logged on a single dive.

faq.q: Dampier Strait, Misool or Wayag - how does a liveaboard week split?
faq.a: Most trips run 7-12 nights to cover the three regions: the Dampier Strait in the centre (Cape Kri, Blue Magic, Sardine Reef, Manta Sandy, Arborek), Misool in the south (Boo Windows, Magic Mountain, Four Kings, Fiabacet) and the Wayag/north karst seascape (Kawe, The Passage). Longer charters reach all three; shorter ones concentrate on Dampier and one wing.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Many of the best sites - Blue Magic, Cape Kri, Sardine Reef - are current-driven drift dives where a reef hook and good buoyancy earn their place; sheltered reefs, jetties (Arborek) and the mangrove channel of The Passage suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards for the repetitive multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the operator briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Raja Ampat liveaboards book?
faq.a: The October-April peak on preferred vessels fills earliest - the dedicated Raja Ampat vessels and luxury phinisi are booked well ahead; hold roughly 6-12 months out for peak windows and marquee boats, nearer term for the shoulder. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for the Egyptian Red Sea, and how do I dive it responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Egypt at Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution (accessed 2026-08-09). The Northern and Middle Sinai Peninsula and parts of the Western Desert carry a Level 4 (Do Not Travel) carve-out; the Red Sea coast sits outside every carve-out, so Hurghada and the northern Red Sea coast carry no sub-zone restriction. The UK FCDO draws the same interior zones in its own words and names no Red Sea resort; the stricter baseline (State Level 2) sets the posture. Carry DAN membership plus separate dive-accident insurance and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: The Red Sea coast runs a dense chamber network. Northern routes are covered by the Hyperbaric Medical Center in Sharm el-Sheikh (DAN Egypt) and HyperMed in Hurghada (next to the airport); southern routes by Baro Medical in Marsa Shagra (about 20 km north of Marsa Alam) and the DECO International chamber in Hamata (a 24-hour recompression and medical-emergency facility about 135 km south of Marsa Alam). Confirm the chamber covering your itinerary and its readiness on your dates via the operator or DAN. Offshore reefs are hours from port, so insurance and a conservative profile matter most there.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive the Red Sea?
faq.a: March-May and September-November are the optimal windows - calm seas, warm water and 30 m+ visibility. Summer (June-August) pushes water to 30C with strong offshore shark action but occasional plankton; winter (December-February) drops to 21-23C and can be windy offshore.

faq.q: When can I see oceanic whitetips, hammerheads and threshers?
faq.a: June-November is the offshore shark window: oceanic whitetips, grey reef and scalloped hammerheads around Daedalus and Elphinstone, with The Brothers known for thresher sharks in the early morning.

faq.q: North route or south route - which liveaboard week?
faq.a: North runs the wrecks and reefs - SS Thistlegorm, Abu Nuhas, Ras Mohammed and the Straits of Tiran (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon). South runs the offshore shark reefs (Brothers, Daedalus, Elphinstone) and the remote Fury Shoals and St John's near the Sudan border; liveaboards favour the calm southern conditions in summer.

faq.q: What certification and conditions should I plan for?
faq.a: The offshore reefs (Brothers, Daedalus, Elphinstone) are current-swept blue-water sites suited to experienced divers; the northern wrecks and Tiran reefs suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on most liveaboards for the repetitive multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the operator briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Red Sea liveaboards book?
faq.a: Peak shark-season southern weeks (June-November) and the marquee wreck routes fill earliest; hold a berth roughly 3-9 months out for peak windows and preferred vessels, with shoulder weeks bookable nearer term. Confirm current per-vessel lead times with the operator.

key_facts: Roatán sits on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second-largest coral-reef system on earth; Bay Islands ranked highest in coral health in the 2015 Mesoamerican assessment.
30+ dive shops on the west side; ~30 named dive sites within a 10-minute boat ride off West Bay/West End, with walls dropping past 100 ft and the El Aguila/Odyssey wrecks.
The Roatán Aggressor IV liveaboard runs Sat->Sat (18 guests, ~24-27 dives) across Roatán, Cayos Cochinos, and Utila.
Whale sharks are snorkel-only and protected; Utila (a short hop from Roatán) offers year-round potential peaking late March-April.
Roatán has an on-island recompression chamber (Cornerstone Hyperbaric, adjacent to Anthony's Key Resort; DAN IPPN partner) — a first-response advantage for wall diving.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: The load-bearing risk is mainland crime, and the plan is to stay in-zone. Violent crime and gang activity concentrate in the San Pedro Sula, Tegucigalpa, and Comayagua corridors, and Gracias a Dios Department carries a Level 4 "Do Not Travel" rating — all on the mainland. Fly direct into RTB, keep the trip airport → island, and never route overland through the gang zones.

faq.q: Is diving Roatán's walls dangerous — and can I fly out afterward?
faq.a: Wall diving rewards depth discipline and respect for the no-fly window, and Roatán has an unusual first-response advantage. Recreational divers work the crest and upper wall (≤60–100 ft); wreck and deep-wall profiles trend technical and are certification-gated. Allow no-fly-after-diving of 18–24 hours before your RTB flight, and note the on-island Cornerstone Hyperbaric Chamber (adjacent to Anthony's Key Resort, a DAN partner) — a genuine safety edge for a wall-diving island. **What makes Roatán's diving special? ** *(Dive Liveaboards / Diving)* Roatán delivers a serious wall reef within minutes of the dock plus a rare repeat-rate track record. Within a 10-minute boat ride off West Bay/West End you reach ~30 named dive sites, from a 15-ft sandy playground with feeding eagle rays to 100-ft+ wall drop-offs, wrecks, and canyon swim-throughs; CoCo View Resort claims the highest repeat rate of any dive resort worldwide (1,600+ guests five times over).

faq.q: How much is the Roatán reef fee, and is it required?
faq.a: Yes, it is mandatory and it is small. The Roatán Marine Park conservation fee is $10/year or $5/day, non-commissionable, and it funds the very reef you came to dive and snorkel — present it as the reef's cover charge, never buried.

faq.q: Is Roatán good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — Roatán runs a genuine adults-only luxury lane on top of the diving. Ibagari Boutique Hotel is adults-only (12+), holds a Michelin Key 2025, and sits between West Bay and West End; private West Bay villas and sunset-cocktail liveaboard finales round out the romance product.

faq.q: Can I snorkel with whale sharks from Roatán?
faq.a: Yes, via a day-trip to neighboring Utila, and only by snorkel. Utila is one of the few places on earth with year-round whale-shark potential, peaking late March–April; the animals are protected, so it is surface snorkeling only — no diving with them and no touching.

faq.q: What are the best beaches and cays on San Andrés?
faq.a: Johnny Cay is the headline — a protected 4-ha coral islet ~1.5 km off San Andrés Town with the best white sand around, reached by colectivo boat — plus calm snorkel pools at La Piscinita and West View, and mellow Rocky Cay off San Luis. The lagoon is the famed "Sea of Seven Colors."

faq.q: Is San Andrés good for scuba diving?
faq.a: Yes — it's a shallow-water reef diver's dream, with 40+ dive sites mostly at ~10–12 m, high-visibility and beginner-friendly, run through island PADI centers like Banda and Sharky. Providencia adds wall diving on the third-largest barrier reef in the world. Note it's day-boat reef diving, not liveaboard-berth product.

faq.q: Is Providencia good for a quiet honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — Providencia is the quiet-honeymoon jewel: near-empty coves, the McBean Lagoon marine park, and Crab Cay (its #1 snorkel spot, ~USD $6 park fee) reached by express boat. It's rebuilt and open after Hurricane Iota (2020); reach it by ~20-minute inter-island flight or catamaran.

faq.q: What language and culture will I find on San Andrés?
faq.a: A living Raizal Afro-Caribbean nation: 20,000–30,000 people speak San Andrés–Providencia Creole (Islander English) and most are trilingual, descended from 18th-century Jamaican settlers and enslaved Africans. The signature plate is rondón — fish, conch and root vegetables simmered in coconut milk.

faq.q: What's the real day-to-day risk on the island?
faq.a: Not the mainland headlines — the island's real risks are petty/beach theft, motorcycle snatch-and-grab, scooter accidents and sea/riptide hazards. Renting a scooter or golf cart is the classic island loop, and scooter crashes plus snatch-and-grab are the two most common tourist mishaps: helmet on, valuables off the seat, drive in daylight.

faq.q: What is the current advisory for the Similan Islands, and how do I dive them responsibly?
faq.a: The U.S. State Department places Thailand at Level 1 - Exercise Normal Precautions nationwide (reissued 7 July 2026). Its Level 2 carve-outs are the Thai-Cambodian border area and the deep-south provinces of Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat - all well away from the Andaman dive coast. The UK FCDO advises against all but essential travel to those southern provinces, parts of Songkhla and within 20 km of the Cambodia border, and names none of Phuket, Khao Lak, Phang Nga or the Similans. The Similan/Surin coast sits outside every carve-out from both; the country baseline (State Level 1) sets the posture. Carry DAN membership plus separate dive-accident insurance and observe an 18-24 hour no-fly window after diving.
faq.source: advisory level reported by nationthailand.com + tvc.co.th citing the US State Dept Thailand advisory reissued 7 Jul 2026 (state.gov 403'd, not read directly); FCDO gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand/regional-risks read via WebFetch 2026-08-09

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: The Similan liveaboard area is comparatively well covered. The SSS Evacuation Center in Khao Lak, on the Tap Lamu departure coast, runs a 24-hour diving-emergency line and serves the Similan fleet directly; behind it, the SSS Recompression Chamber in Phuket - southern Thailand's first diver chamber (established 1996), a multiplace chamber taking up to four occupants - operates 24/7 and covers the whole west coast from the Myanmar border to Malaysia. Confirm current contacts and readiness through the operator or DAN before your trip.

faq.q: When can I dive the Similans, and when are whale sharks and mantas most likely?
faq.a: The season is fixed by the national parks: liveaboards run October-May, and the Similan and Surin parks close in the southwest monsoon (about mid-May to mid-October). Within the season, manta and whale-shark encounters at Richelieu Rock, Koh Bon and Koh Tachai are most associated with the February-April plankton-rich weeks, though sightings are never guaranteed.

faq.q: Which sites define a Similan liveaboard week?
faq.a: Richelieu Rock (the marquee), the manta and pelagic pinnacles of Koh Bon and Koh Tachai, and the Similan granite sites - Elephant Head Rock, Christmas Point, West of Six, Boulder City and East of Eden - with the Boon Sung wreck off Khao Lak as a muck-and-macro finale. Longer trips add the Surin Islands.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: Koh Bon, Koh Tachai and Richelieu Rock are current-swept pinnacles best suited to experienced divers; the Similan boulder sites and the Boon Sung wreck suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on liveaboards for the repetitive multi-day profile. Dive within your certification and the operator briefing.

faq.q: How far ahead do Similan liveaboards book?
faq.a: Because the season is short and park-gated, the marquee boats and the February-April pelagic weeks fill earliest; hold roughly 4-9 months out for peak windows and preferred vessels, nearer term for the season edges. Confirm per-vessel lead times with the operator.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Statia?
faq.a: Dive discipline and remoteness. Hold the no-fly 18-24h window; Statia has an on-island recompression chamber, but the local hospital is small - serious cases route to St. Maarten (~18-min flight), so travel insurance with evacuation cover is wise.

faq.q: When is the best time to dive Statia?
faq.a: Diving is year-round (warm, clear, quiet), but Statia IS in the hurricane belt - favour December-April (dry, reliable) and be weather-aware August-October (peak storm months).

faq.q: Do I need permits for Statia, and what do they cost?
faq.a: Yes - a STENAPA marine tag for diving and a $10 hiking permit for the Quill/Boven trails, both funding conservation; buy them through your dive centre or STENAPA.

faq.q: Which Statia sites and experiences should I not miss?
faq.a: The heritage reefs over cannons and anchors, the award-winning macro life, the island's wreck dives, a Quill crater hike, and historic Oranjestad with Fort Oranje - a rare dive-plus-history pairing.

faq.q: Is Statia a liveaboard destination?
faq.a: No - it's a shore-and-day-boat heritage-dive island. Liveaboards may route past Statia on St. Kitts itineraries, but there is no Statia-based liveaboard - book a resort-and-dive-centre trip.
