faq.q: What is the current advisory for Tubbataha, and why is it not bookable here?
faq.a: The Philippines carries a U.S. State Department Level 2 - Exercise Increased Caution rating nationwide (reissued 8 May 2025, with a Kidnapping 'K' indicator). The advisory also designates a Level 4 (Do Not Travel) zone - 'The Sulu Archipelago, including the southern Sulu Sea, due to crime, terrorism, civil unrest, and kidnapping.' The UK FCDO (reissued 1 April 2026) advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago. Tubbataha sits in the Sulu Sea, administratively Cagayancillo, Palawan, roughly 150 km southeast of Puerto Princesa. The advisory names 'the southern Sulu Sea' as Level 4 but never draws that zone's boundary and does not mention Tubbataha; no park-authority, UNESCO or operator source resolves it either. Because the park's position relative to the Level 4 zone could not be established from any source that draws the line, TravelWell holds this destination as content-only and does not offer it as bookable until the question is resolved with the park authority against the live advisory.
faq.source: State L4 wording confirmed via childabduction.state.gov mirror 2026-08-10; L2/K + FCDO 1 Apr 2026 supplied by Strategy Claude from a 2026-08-09 read of travel.state.gov + gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/philippines

faq.q: Is there a recompression chamber, and how remote is care?
faq.a: Care is remote and the sources disagree, so treat this as not verifiable as of 2026-08-10. Some operators cite a chamber at the city hospital in Puerto Princesa, Palawan, roughly 10-12 hours away by boat; one dive guide names Cebu City instead; and Master Liveaboards lists facilities at Batangas, Manila, Cebu and Subic reached by private air evacuation, without naming Puerto Princesa. No source confirms a 24-hour operational status. DAN membership and dive-accident insurance with air-evacuation cover are essential.

faq.q: When can I dive Tubbataha?
faq.a: Only in the mid-March to mid-June window, when park authorities open the season for the calmest weather; exact dates are set each year by the Tubbataha Management Office. It is liveaboard-only - no shore access and no night diving - with boats running from Puerto Princesa.

faq.q: What will I see underwater?
faq.a: The park is recorded at hundreds of coral and fish species; grey reef sharks appear on nearly every dive, typically in groups, alongside whitetips and - depending on the day - hammerheads, thresher and whale sharks, mantas, and nesting hawksbill and green turtles.

faq.q: Which sites define a Tubbataha week?
faq.a: Shark Airport for the grey-reef aggregation, the Delsan and Malayan wrecks, the walls at Black Rock, Southwest Wall and the North and South Atolls, Staghorn Point and Ko-ok, and the isolated Jessie Beazley Reef to the north.

faq.q: What conditions and certification should I plan for?
faq.a: The atoll walls and Jessie Beazley are current-swept blue-water dives suited to experienced divers; sheltered reef tops suit a wider range with a guide. Nitrox is standard on the liveaboards. Dive within your certification and the operator briefing.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Tulum?
faq.a: Sargassum above all — Tulum is the worst-hit beach stretch on the Riviera Maya, and 2026 is a record year, so beach quality is genuinely not guaranteed. Anchor the trip on ruins, cenotes and Sian Ka'an rather than a pristine-beach promise. Also plan for hurricane season (Jun–Nov), bottled water, and dengue (peak May–Nov, no malaria).

faq.q: Is cenote and cave diving in Tulum dangerous?
faq.a: It demands the right certification for serious overhead-environment diving. Sistema Sac Actun and Dos Ojos are caves: cavern diving requires a certified cave/cavern guide and must stay in the daylight zone, and the dark cave zone requires full cave certification — no exceptions, no solo penetration. Observe no-fly of 18h single / 24h repetitive; the nearest chamber is ~60 km north.

faq.q: When should I visit the Tulum ruins?
faq.a: Right at the 8am opening. The archaeological zone runs 8am–5pm (last entry 3:30pm), and the 8–10am window beats both the heat and the crowds at this cliff-top walled city. Come in November or February for low crowds and ideal temperatures; Holy Week (2026: Mar 29–Apr 5) runs at full capacity and Apr–Oct heat is intense.

faq.q: What are the best cenotes for diving near Tulum?
faq.a: Gran Cenote and Dos Ojos lead — Tulum sits above Sistema Sac Actun, a ~347 km interconnected cave system, the densest cenote country in Mexico. Gran Cenote (2.5 mi from town) is an all-levels swim/snorkel/intro-dive; Dos Ojos is the marquee guided cavern dive. All are weather-independent and sargassum-immune, making them the reliable core of a Tulum trip.

faq.q: Will sargassum ruin the Tulum beaches in 2026?
faq.a: Be realistic: Tulum is the worst-hit stretch on the coast, its open Atlantic-facing beaches catch the full brunt, and 2026 is a record/near-record year — beach quality is not guaranteed. Don't cancel; re-anchor. Build the trip on ruins, cenotes and the Sian Ka'an biosphere (all sargassum-proof), and for reliable sand, the Punta Maroma stretch ~1 hour north sits north of the worst.

faq.q: What is Tulum's wellness scene like?
faq.a: It is Tulum's defining draw — yoga, temazcal ceremonies, cenote healing and jungle spas concentrated along the beach road. A signature is a north-Tulum cove with a beachfront cenote where you swim fresh and salt water in one spot, paired with jungle wellness. Book through a boutique hotel or DMC; some of the best programs are direct-only.

faq.q: Is Tulum good for a honeymoon, and where's the luxury?
faq.a: Yes — it is a honeymoon icon, built on bohemian-luxe boutiques and staffed villas. On the beach road, design icons like Azulik and Our Habitas Tulum lead (many are direct-only — verify the channel); for branded ultra beyond the sargassum, Maroma (A Belmond Hotel) and the 70-villa Chablé Maroma sit ~1 hour north. Fully staffed beach villas are the top private rung.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Tulum, and how far ahead do I book?
faq.a: November–April is the dry high season; November and February are the best value inside it (roughly 15–25% below peak), with November the single best month (dry, minimal seaweed, pre-holiday prices). Peak weeks run 40–60% above shoulder — reserve Christmas/NYE by September and Feb–March by November, as the boutique scene sells out months ahead.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for?
faq.a: Two risks are load-bearing: mainland crime and island remoteness. The advisory names Gracias a Dios Department (Level 4 "Do Not Travel") and urban mainland gang zones — all away from Utila, so keep the client in-zone (airport → ferry/charter → island). Separately, serious trauma or complex dive injuries route off-island to La Ceiba then a mainland hospital or US medevac, so carry travel-medical, air-evac, and DAN dive insurance without exception.

faq.q: Is learning to dive here dangerous, and can I fly out afterward?
faq.a: Diving here rewards a certified operator and disciplined profiles, and Utila has an unusual on-island safety asset. Certify only with a PADI/SSI-certified shop (UDC, Alton's, Parrots, College of Diving, Underwater Vision), dive within no-decompression limits, and observe no-fly-after-diving of 18–24 hours before flying. Utila has its own hyperbaric chamber at Utila Lodge (doubling as the island trauma center), with a chamber also via Bay Islands College of Diving — a genuine asset most small dive islands lack.

faq.q: Why is Utila the cheapest place to learn to dive?
faq.a: Utila built its name as the place backpackers came to get certified for a few hundred dollars and never left. A PADI/SSI Open Water course runs roughly US$280–350 — among the cheapest on Earth — with free or discounted dorm accommodation while you dive, on a reef with 60+ dive sites a few fin-kicks off the dock.

faq.q: Can I dive with the whale sharks, or only snorkel?
faq.a: Snorkel only — scuba diving with whale sharks is prohibited. As a protected species they are approached from the surface during surface intervals: captains hunt the "boil/roil" of feeding fish and diving birds, and you drop off the boat and snorkel beside them. Sightings are probabilistic (best odds Mar–May and Aug–Sep) — market "best odds," never a guarantee.

faq.q: What is there to do on Utila besides diving?
faq.a: Plenty above the water, all budget-friendly. Take a boat to Water Cay's uninhabited white-sand sandbar, cold cans at Chepes Beach (the island's largest public beach), the Utila Cays Garífuna fishing village of Jewel Cay and Pigeon (~500 people on stilt homes over the water), and Freedive Utila — Central America's first freediving training center — where you learn to fall through the blue on one breath.
